resultJson.summary: Fix vert.x cats fs2 streaming deadlock when the Dispatcher runs on a small fixed thread pool

entries.resultJson:
I added the failing test at `server/vertx-server/cats/src/test/scala/sttp/tapir/server/vertx/cats/CatsVertxLimitedThreadPoolStreamingTest.scala`, and it fails on the current code, which confirms the bug.

**What the test does:**
- It uses plain cats-effect `IO`, not ZIO. It builds a custom `IORuntime` whose compute pool is `Executors.newFixedThreadPool(2)`. Unlike cats-effect's default thread pool, this pool can't add threads when some are blocked, which matches the ZIO executor in the issue.
- It starts a Vert.x server with a streaming endpoint whose server logic sleeps 200ms and then returns an fs2 stream.
- It sends 2 concurrent requests from the test thread with `HttpClient.sendAsync` and waits at most 20s. The timeout is on the test thread, so the test fails rather than hangs.

**Result** (`vertxServerCats3/testOnly ...CatsVertxLimitedThreadPoolStreamingTest`): it fails with a `TimeoutException` after 20s. When the pool is shut down in cleanup, the log shows the compute threads were stuck in `Await.result`, i.e. `Dispatcher.unsafeRunSync` inside `fs2ReadStreamCompatible.mapToReadStream`. That is the deadlock from the issue.

The test also compiles on Scala 2.13 with no warnings. I only ran it on Scala 3.

To make the test pass, `mapToReadStream` should stop blocking a thread with `unsafeRunSync`, as the issue suggests.

resultJson.description:
Fix softwaremill/tapir#5458: the Vert.x cats server interpreter freezes when the effect runtime uses a fixed-size compute pool (e.g. ZIO's executor via zio-interop-cats) and as many streaming requests arrive concurrently as there are compute threads. Cause: the fs2 `ReadStreamCompatible` in `server/vertx-server/cats/.../streams/fs2.scala` calls `dispatcher.unsafeRunSync` to set up its stream bridges and inside the Vert.x ReadStream callbacks. For response bodies this runs inside the request's own `F` effect, which already occupies a compute thread; `unsafeRunSync` parks that thread until the dispatcher can run the submitted effect on another compute thread. Once every compute thread is parked this way nothing can progress. The request-body/WebSocket-input bridge (`fromReadStreamInternal`) has the identical shape and is also entered from inside `F`.

Goal: remove every thread-blocking `unsafeRunSync` from the fs2 bridge so no code path in the cats interpreter blocks a compute or Vert.x event-loop thread waiting on the dispatcher. Setup that only creates state and forks a fiber becomes plain JVM state (`AtomicReference`, `Deferred.unsafe`) plus `dispatcher.unsafeRunAndForget` of a forked effect; Vert.x callbacks mutate state synchronously and fire-and-forget only the resulting deferred completions. Ordering and back-pressure semantics must be preserved and the result must work with both `Dispatcher.parallel` and `Dispatcher.sequential`. The committed `CatsVertxLimitedThreadPoolStreamingTest` must pass, and `Fs2StreamTest` plus the full `CatsVertxServerTest` suite (streaming and WebSocket) must keep passing on Scala 2.13 and 3. The ZIO Vert.x module has the same pattern but is out of scope.

tasks.title: Make the fs2 response/WebSocket-output bridge (mapToReadStream) non-blocking
tasks.description:
In `server/vertx-server/cats/src/main/scala/sttp/tapir/server/vertx/cats/streams/fs2.scala`, rewrite `mapToReadStream` so it never calls `opts.dispatcher.unsafeRunSync`:
- Hold `StreamState[F, O]` in an `AtomicReference`, initialised with `StreamState.empty(Deferred.unsafe[F, Unit])` (wrapped via the existing `DeferredOps`).
- Start the draining stream with `opts.dispatcher.unsafeRunAndForget(<existing evalMap/onFinalizeCase pipeline>.compile.drain.start.void)`. Inside the stream read state via `Sync[F].delay(state.get)`; keep the paused/re-read-after-wake logic and the three finalize cases unchanged.
- `handler`/`endHandler`/`exceptionHandler`: synchronous `updateAndGet`. `pause()`: create `Deferred.unsafe[F, Unit]` and set it only if not already paused. `resume()`: `getAndUpdate(_.copy(paused = None))`, then if the old state had a deferred, `opts.dispatcher.unsafeRunAndForget(deferred.complete(()))`. `fetch` stays a no-op.
- Remove now-unused imports.
Verify: `CatsVertxLimitedThreadPoolStreamingTest` passes; `Fs2StreamTest` and `CatsVertxServerTest` pass on `vertxServerCats3`; `vertxServerCats2_13` compiles without warnings and its tests pass.

tasks.title: Make the fs2 request-body/WebSocket-input bridge (fromReadStreamInternal) non-blocking, with a request-side regression test
tasks.description:
In the same fs2.scala, rewrite `fromReadStreamInternal` so neither its setup nor the Vert.x callbacks block:
- Hold `ReadStreamState[F, T]` in an `AtomicReference`. In the two `unfoldEval` loops replace `stateRef.modify(f)` with `Sync[F].delay(Pipe.modify(ref, f))` (`sttp.tapir.server.vertx.streams.Pipe`), keeping `mbAction.traverse(identity)` and the Pause/Resume `.attempt.void` handling.
- Start the activation-event pump with `opts.dispatcher.unsafeRunAndForget(pump.compile.drain.start.void)`; register the Vert.x handlers and return the consumer stream synchronously.
- `endHandler`/`exceptionHandler`/`handler`: compute state and actions synchronously with `Pipe.modify(ref, _.halt(...))` / `Pipe.modify(ref, _.enqueue(buffer, opts.maxQueueSizeForReadStream))`, then, if the action list is non-empty, `opts.dispatcher.unsafeRunAndForget(actions.sequence_)`. Add a one-line comment that the synchronous modify is what keeps buffer order under a parallel dispatcher.
- Add a second test to `CatsVertxLimitedThreadPoolStreamingTest` (extract the runtime/server setup shared with the first test): a POST endpoint with `.in(streamTextBody(Fs2Streams[IO])(CodecFormat.TextPlain(), None)).out(stringBody)`, a `serverSecurityLogic` that sleeps 200ms (the body, and thus `toStream`, is decoded only after security logic, so both requests enter the bridge at the same time), and a main logic that reads the stream to a String. Send 2 concurrent POSTs with a short body and assert both are echoed within 20s.
Verify: both tests in `CatsVertxLimitedThreadPoolStreamingTest` pass; `Fs2StreamTest` (including the `pauseCount`/`resumeCount` expectations) and `CatsVertxServerTest` pass on `vertxServerCats3`; `vertxServerCats2_13` compiles without warnings and its tests pass.

resultJson.brief:
## Modules and files
- `server/vertx-server/` (sbt `vertxServer`): effect-agnostic core.
  - `streams/ReadStreamCompatible.scala`: bridge trait (`asReadStream`, `fromReadStream`, `webSocketPipe`).
  - `streams/domain.scala`: shared state types, all `private[vertx]` and shared with the ZIO module; do not change. `StreamState[F, T](paused: Option[DeferredLike[F, Unit]], handler: Handler[T], errorHandler: Handler[Throwable], endHandler: Handler[Void])`, `StreamState.empty(promise)` starts paused. `ReadStreamState[F, C](buffers, activationEvents)` with pure methods `enqueue(chunk, maxSize): (state, List[F[Unit]])`, `halt(cause): (state, List[F[Unit]])`, `dequeueBuffer(dfd)`, `dequeueActivationEvent(dfd)`; the `List[F[Unit]]` are deferred completions to run after the atomic state change. `DeferredLike[F, A] { complete(a): F[Unit]; get: F[A] }`.
  - `streams/Pipe.scala`: pumps a Vert.x `ReadStream` into a `WriteStream`/WebSocket; registers `handler`, `endHandler`, `exceptionHandler` then calls `resume()` immediately, all synchronously. Exposes public `Pipe.modify[A, B](ref: AtomicReference[A], f: A => (A, B)): B` (CAS loop, same shape as `Ref.modify`).
  - `encoders/VertxToResponseBody.scala#fromStreamValue`: calls `asReadStream(v)` then `Pipe(readStream, rc.response)` inside the request's `F`.
  - `decoders/VertxRequestBody.scala#toStream`: calls `fromReadStream(rc.request, maxBytes)` inside `F`.
- `server/vertx-server/cats/` (sbt `vertxServerCats`; project ids `vertxServerCats2_13`, `vertxServerCats3`): the cats interpreter. Only file to change: `src/main/scala/sttp/tapir/server/vertx/cats/streams/fs2.scala`. `VertxCatsServerInterpreter#endpointHandler` runs each request via `dispatcher.unsafeRunCancelable(result)` from the event loop (non-blocking, leave as is). `VertxCatsServerOptions.dispatcher: Dispatcher[F]` is user-supplied (parallel or sequential); `maxQueueSizeForReadStream: Int` (default 16).
- `server/core/.../interpreter/ServerInterpreter.scala`: security inputs are decoded and `securityLogic` run (line ~124) before the main body is decoded (line ~145), and the body decode is where `requestBody.toStream` is called. A sleep in `serverSecurityLogic` therefore delays `toStream` deterministically.
- Tests, `server/vertx-server/cats/src/test/scala/sttp/tapir/server/vertx/cats/`:
  - `CatsVertxLimitedThreadPoolStreamingTest.scala` (committed repro, AnyFunSuite): builds an `IORuntime` on `Executors.newFixedThreadPool(2)`, starts a Vert.x server with a GET `/stream` endpoint whose logic sleeps 200ms then returns an fs2 stream, sends 2 concurrent GETs via Java `HttpClient.sendAsync`, waits 20s. Currently fails with `TimeoutException`.
  - `streams/Fs2StreamTest.scala` (AsyncFlatSpec): unit tests for `asReadStream` (pause/resume/end/error) and `fromReadStream` (drain, back-pressure `pauseCount`/`resumeCount`, failure) using `sttp.tapir.server.vertx.streams.FakeStream` from the core module's test sources.
  - `CatsVertxServerTest.scala`: full shared suite incl. `ServerStreamingTests` and `ServerWebSocketTests`; `retries = 3`; forces HTTP/1.

## Deadlock mechanism (verified)
`mapToReadStream` (fs2.scala:42) wraps `Deferred` + `Ref.of(StreamState.empty)` + `GenSpawn[F].start(stream.compile.drain)` in `opts.dispatcher.unsafeRunSync`, which submits to the dispatcher and `Await.result`s on the calling thread. Called from inside the request's `F` on a compute thread, each streaming response parks one compute thread waiting for another; N concurrent requests on an N-thread pool deadlock. The returned `ReadStream`'s `handler/endHandler/exceptionHandler/pause/resume` each `unsafeRunSync` too, and `Pipe.apply` calls all of them right after `asReadStream` on the same thread. `fromReadStreamInternal` (fs2.scala:119) has the same setup shape (entered via `toStream` and `webSocketPipe`), and its Vert.x callbacks (lines 166-173) `unsafeRunSync` on the event-loop thread.

## Key APIs (cats-effect 3.7.1, fs2 3.14.0)
- `Dispatcher[F]`: `unsafeRunSync` (blocking, remove all uses in fs2.scala), `unsafeRunAndForget[A](fa: F[A]): Unit` (non-blocking).
- `Deferred.unsafe[F[_]: Async, A]: Deferred[F, A]` creates a Deferred without running `F`; fs2.scala's `implicit class DeferredOps[F[_]: Async, A](dfd: Deferred[F, A]) extends DeferredLike[F, A]` adapts it. `Ref.unsafe` does not help: its `update` still returns `F`. Use `java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicReference` (`updateAndGet`, `getAndUpdate`, `Pipe.modify`).
- Vert.x `ReadStream[T]` setters return `this`.

## Semantics to preserve
- Forking: submit `effect.start.void` to `unsafeRunAndForget`, never the raw `compile.drain`; with `Dispatcher.sequential` a long-running submission would block all later submissions, including request handling. The old code forked inside the submission too, and the fiber was never joined or cancelled; keep that.
- Ordering: `Dispatcher.parallel` does not order `unsafeRunAndForget` calls. Vert.x delivers buffers in order, so enqueue/halt state mutation must be synchronous on the calling thread; only the returned completions get dispatched. Each queue holds at most one pending Deferred (`Empty(dfd)`), so async completion cannot reorder data.
- `resume()`: clear `paused` synchronously, then complete the old deferred (fire-and-forget). `pause()`: never replace an existing `paused` deferred. The stream fiber re-reads state after waking (existing comment explains why); keep it.
- Keep the `.attempt.void` around `readStream.pause()/resume()` (Vert.x 5 throws `IllegalStateException` on a fully-read request).

## Conventions
- Run: `sbt "vertxServerCats3/testOnly sttp.tapir.server.vertx.cats.CatsVertxLimitedThreadPoolStreamingTest"` (project id confirmed); also compile and test `vertxServerCats2_13`. Remove imports that become unused (`Ref`, `GenSpawn`); unused-import warnings matter on 2.13.
- Never commit; no Claude co-author. Comments only for non-obvious reasoning, never restating code. Match the existing test style.
- Java `HttpClient` may try an h2c upgrade; if a POST test misbehaves, use `HttpClient.newBuilder().version(HttpClient.Version.HTTP_1_1)` (the shared suite forces HTTP/1 for the same reason).
- `.orca/` is tooling state; ignore.

id.name: Task: Make the fs2 response/WebSocket-output bridge (mapToReadStream) non-blocking

reason.text: It isn't redundant. With Dispatcher.sequential, submitting the long-running compile.drain directly would block every later submission, including request handling. Keeping the stream detached also matches the old GenSpawn.start behaviour. The new comment (I3.1) explains this.
